subject: MSA & Order Form: liability cap, SLA credits, and sole-remedy language
messages:
From: Beth Dawson <beth.dawson@acme.com>

Cc: Acme Legal <safeguard-legal@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft MSA/Order Form - liability language questions

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for sending the draft. Our GC has a few open items on the MSA and Order Form around limitation of liability and how SLA credits interact with the cap/sole-remedy language. High-level:

- We need clarity on whether SLA credits are the "sole and exclusive remedy" for downtime, and if so, whether that precludes other remedies for consequential damages stemming from an outage.
- We expect carve-outs for willful misconduct and data breach (we can't accept those inside a simple dollar cap).
- Clarify whether credits can be paid in addition to other remedies or only as an offset.

I'm attaching our annotated MSA (redlined_MSA_acme_v2.docx) and a marked-up Order Form. Can your legal team confirm Redwood's position and propose a workable compromise?

We'd prefer to resolve this before procurement routing — ideally by early next week. Happy to jump on a short call if easier.

Best,
Beth

Beth —

Thanks for the clear notes and the redlines. I've looped in Karthik from Legal and Marissa on the commercial side so we can align on redline language and the commercial cap mechanics. Quick read:

- Redwood's starting position: general cap = 12 months of fees (Order Form MRR * 12), exclusions for IP indemnity and breaches that result from our negligence/willful misconduct.
- For SLA credits: we typically designate credits as the sole remedy for availability-related issues, but we understand Acme's concern about interaction with data/security events. We can draft a carve-out so credits are sole remedy for pure availability incidents, while not limiting recovery for data breaches or indemnifiable claims.
- Credit cap: commercially we often cap aggregate credits in a 12-month period (e.g., up to 50% of MRR in aggregate or a 1x monthly cap per incident). Happy to propose specific numbers.

Next steps: Karthik — can you draft suggested replacement language for the MSA + a short note explaining how the Order Form credit mechanics (per-incidence cap, annual cap, offset rules) relate to the general liability cap? Marissa — can you confirm the commercial acceptable ranges so I can communicate them to Acme?

If Acme would prefer, we can do a 30-min call Thursday to walk live through the redline.

—Jordan

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 23 Jul 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: Draft MSA/Order Form - liability language questions (proposed redline)

Jordan / Marissa —

Draft replacement language below (for insertion into Section 8 of the MSA and the Order Form interaction clause). This is legal's starting compromise; please review and call out any commercial constraints.

Proposed clause (short form):
"Limitations of Liability and Exclusive Remedies. Except for (a) Customer's payment obligations, (b) Redwood's indemnification obligations for third-party IP claims, and (c) liability arising from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct or Redwood's failure to comply with its Data Security obligations, Redwood's aggregate liability under this Agreement shall not exceed the amount equal to the fees paid by Customer to Redwood in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to liability.

Notwithstanding the foregoing, for Service Availability incidents governed by the Order Form SLA, Customer's sole and exclusive remedy for Service Availability failures shall be the SLA credits set forth in the Order Form; provided that (i) SLA credits for a given month shall not exceed one (1) times the monthly recurring charges for the affected service, and (ii) aggregate SLA credits in any rolling 12-month period shall not exceed fifty percent (50%) of the monthly recurring charges. The foregoing sole remedy for Service Availability shall not limit Customer's rights with respect to (A) claims arising from Data Security incidents, or (B) claims for fraud, willful misconduct, or gross negligence."
Notes:
- The language keeps SLA credits as the exclusive remedy for pure availability lapses while expressly excluding data security incidents and the most serious Redwood misconduct from the cap.
- Commercially, we can be flexible on the per-incident cap (1x MRR) vs. per-month cap; Marissa can advise.
- We should add a short explanatory redline in the Order Form so Acme sees exactly how credit calculations feed into the cap.

I'll attach a quick text file with the sanitized clause (proposed_sla_text.txt) and a mark-up of the MSA with tracked changes.

—Karthik

Subject: Re: Draft MSA/Order Form - liability language questions

Jordan / Karthik —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A few points from our GC after reviewing Karthik's language:

- We cannot accept a blanket "sole and exclusive" remedy if it completely prevents recovery for downstream business interruption caused by prolonged outages. We would agree to SLA credits as the primary remedy for short outages, but we want an ability to seek consequential damages if outages (or repeated failures) result in material business loss.
- We absolutely need the data-security carve-out (agreed). We also want to be explicit that the cap does not apply to amounts payable as indemnity for breaches of Customer Data obligations.
- Regarding the credit caps: 50% aggregate in 12 months feels low for us. Proposal: per-incident cap = 1x MRR, aggregate cap = 100% of annual MRR, with a mechanism to escalate to a higher cap if there is a clear pattern of service instability.

Can Redwood propose language that preserves SLA credits as an efficient remediation for availability incidents but preserves customer rights for material repeated outages (e.g., a threshold-triggered exception to the sole remedy if three severe incidents occur in a 90-day window)?

If helpful, we can do a 30-min call Friday morning to align.

Best,
Beth

Beth —

Appreciate the specificity — that's helpful. Proposed path forward:

1) Redwood legal will update the clause to include a limited "pattern" exception: if Customer experiences three (3) Severity 1 incidents in a ninety (90)-day rolling window, the sole-remedy limitation for Service Availability will not apply for damages directly resulting from those incidents (subject to standard causation and mitigation). This creates a clear trigger for when consequential recovery becomes available.

2) Commercial caps: we can move to your commercial proposal as a negotiation starting point: per-incident cap = 1x MRR, annual aggregate cap = 100% of annual MRR. We'll call out that credits remain the primary remedy for availability, with the pattern-triggered exception described above.

3) Data security and IP indemnity still fall outside the 12-month general liability cap.

I'll attach the updated redline (redlined_MSA_acme_v2.docx — revised) and a short Order Form exhibit that shows credit calculation examples. Can we schedule Friday 10:00am PT for a 30-min call to walk Acme Legal and Procurement through the compromise? If that works, I'll send a calendar invite and a DocuSign link for the updated Order Form once we align.

Thanks — looking forward to wrapping this.
